sections.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or in the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.

Having reached the worlds where the righteous dwell, and having remained there for many years, he who has slipped from the path of spirituality will be born again in the family of the pure, benevolent and prosperous.
Or, he may be born in the family of the wise sages, though a birth like this is, indeed, very difficult to obtain.

So we had been discussing Chapter 6, Dhyana Yoga, Yoga of Meditation. And obviously this is the conclusion of all the discussion we had about ourselves, who we are, what we consider ourselves to be, what we should be considering ourselves to be and how to get there. Right now Im identified with this limited being called me, my body, mind and intellect.
Chapter two said, your goal is to identify with the one which is imperishable. Then we have talked about how to do this through Karma Yoga by doing greater good selfless activities to purify your mind and intellectual so that it starts seeing the reality as is without coloring it through your vasanas and desires and aspirations and goals. And then when I go through that process, we had been told how to now train your mind to not go outside.
So wherever our mind goes, thats where our attachment goes. Thats where identification is. My mind goes to my leg.
And therefore my identification is more stronger with the body at the time. Nothing, no great ideas are important that time. Look, my leg is hurting.
Let me tell you about theory of evolution. So wherever a mind goes, thats where my identification is. Mind has now tendency to go out in this world and attach do many things create new attachments every day.
So we learned that the goal is now to withdraw the mind, make it inward towards yourself and attach it to yourself. When we get to that point, what will be our experience and we have Learned in verse 29 says Sarva Bhutastam Atmanam Sarva Bhutani Chaatma. Right now I think this is me.
I am in the center of my world. You are in the center of your world. She is in the center of her world.
He is in the center of his world. And whenever world collides, thats our relationship. Sometimes they overlaps in a pleasant way and we have friendly encounter.
Sometimes they collide very violently and we have conflicts. When my goal and your goal is to achieve the same object, then we are on a collision course as we see in the debates last night, in the very first debate when there are 15 candidates, Donald Trump said, Ted Cruz is a good guy. He is not capable, but he is my friend.
Gradually yesterday, he is a liar. He is a liar, nothing but a liar. They are both going toward the same object and they are on a collision course.
So our worlds are separate and they come and collide with each other in various ways because we all have different worlds. But once the mind is turned towards inward, Bhagavan said, you will find that the self which you call yourself is not only just yourself, but the same self in all the beings. There are not too many different selves, the one self expressing through all the beings.
So therefore, Sarva Bhutastam Atmanam I see that this same self is residing in all the beings. What I consider my consciousness is the same consciousness for you and him and she and her. In Sarva Bhutani Ch.
Aatmani not only that, I will also see that the self is not in the beings. Actually, the beings are in the self. Our standard analogy, the this space is in this room.
The next door room has its own space. So this room space and that room space have some relationship. They belong to the same building.
So they are basically related to each other more friendly way. So this space and that space, how did I create them? By putting a partition between in the space, the one space. I put a partition created two space.
Now did I really divide the space or I put a partition in the space? I actually put the partition in the space space remaining what it is, I just put a partition in. So now is it the space within the partitions or the partitions are within the space? Those of you who have been attending Gita class for a long time know that the partition is in the space. This room used to be much larger partition.
The same way, when I start visualizing that all these buildings in this world are actually in the space, not that the space is in the building. So when I turn my gaze towards myself, not only I find that my self is something other than this body, mind and intellect, but the same self is expressing through all the body. All the beings and all the beings are nothing but in the space.
Because the self is all pervading, just as the space is all pervading. So no matter what building I create in, no matter where on this planet or in another universe, its still the same space. Iksate Yoga Yukta Tma, Sarvatraha Samadharsanaha One who has become the Yoga Yukta.
One who has mastered the yoga. Yoga is to connect one who has mastered that connection of removing this identification from this outside world to inside. Sarvatra Samadarsana. He becomes equanimous in all his vision.
His mind is at equanimity. No matter what the situation is, he sees the same reality. The goal is to reach a stage where you start seeing that myself is the same as yourself.
Yourself is same as his self and herself. And now all beings are nothing but the expression of same self. So Arjuna had a doubt.
This looks like a pipe dream to me. This looks like something far fetched somewhere. Because the very goal is to turn the mind towards itself.
Detaching it from all the attachments it has. That really does not seem like a very viable proposition. So get a doubt and say, I dont see this happening.
This mind is so chanchal then so unstable that it is like trying to control wind. We all know that controlling wind is not something in our hand. No matter how much technological advances we are.
When hurricane comes, all you can do is just watch on tv. But you cannot really control. You can say, let me now turn the hurricanes path.
So the mind is like that hurricane. Typically our mind is in a turbulent shape. Its not easy to control.
Then Bhagavan said, thats correct. That mind is Chanchala Nasthir but Abhyasena. By constant practice it can be tamed.
The circus animals, they are tamed to do some amazing things. Elephants standing on two legs, you know, Dog jumping through fire. By constant practice even this mind can be tamed.
The circus animals can be tamed. Your mind also can be tamed by practice and Vairagyana and by dispassion. More you detach from outside.
More you detach from your body. More you detach from your intellect. Mind is free to go and attach to the self.
More I am as I consider me today. More difficult it is for mind to go and attach it to the self. He said Abhyasena in Vairagyana, two pointers given by Bhagavan.
Mind cannot be tamed. Bhagavan said, no, it can be. Dont underestimate the power of your mind.
That its Pramathini. Even any powerful thing also can be tamed. So we Talked about the hydro power Water, when it is flooding, has a great capacity to create destruction.
The same water can be tamed into a hydro dam and create energy. So the same mind which has this tremendous energy to take you away from your goal, that same energy can be harnessed and cultivated to find yourself. Bhaiya Vyasayana vairagya.
The two pointers Bhagwangya. So it dispelled his doubt. Narjuna has a different doubt.
So he says, and these doubts are very universal. These doubts are universal. In the path of seeking the truth, every seeker comes to seek doubt.
First thing we hear is this chapter is great, but meditation is not easy. So Bhagavan said, okay, if you are really serious, keep trying. Keep trying and keep trying and try and try again, boys.
You will succeed at last. You know, you will continue trying and you will achieve that. Now is another doubt because we know that this life is limited.
Just looking at all the things which is happening. We have one of our friend died last week. Biswanath Basu went to India.
He wrote back saying his father went to surgery: Thank you very much for prayers. And yesterday he sent a note saying his father passed away. So people feel they may have very little time left. Rajan, finish all the podcasts -- what do we want to do? Quickly move on. Now Arjuna, in verse 37: Ayatih shraddhaya upetah -- I have complete faith.
I have faith that this is right, this is the path I must be following. That is not a problem. Intellectually Im convinced this is the right path.
My goal is to find the truth myself. But ayatih -- because of the uncontrolled self, no control over my senses. Yoga chalita manasah -- the mind wavers away from this yoga. Every new year we make resolutions. I said, I dont have much time left. My passion is singing, and I know Im getting old, my voice is going.
So I said, let me practice before my voice goes away, maybe record another album. And then after a while I fall into the same pattern: Theres not enough time. Architecture practice is more important. So even though I have faith and a goal, the mind wavers away from this yoga -- Yoga chalita manasah -- and attaches itself to other things.
Aprapya yoga samsiddhim -- so he is not achieving. I have not achieved the Yoga Samsiddhim. I have not achieved the perfection in yoga. Kam gatim Krishna gacchati -- what happens to that person? He had all the faith, he was trying hard, but because of uncontrolled senses and mind, he wandered away from the yoga, and he dies.
Time is over, time is up. Kacchit na ubhaya vibhrashtah chinna abhram iva nashyati -- doesnt he get destroyed like the torn cloud, the shattered cloud? Our basic dilemma is: should I be focusing on my materialistic world and achieve accomplishments there, or should I be pursuing the path of spirituality? If I just focus on one, maybe I can get success. But doing both may not be possible.
When we came to this town and we started these classes, a couple of our friends who made new friends, they said Rajan, they are businessmen, said Rajan, as much time you are putting in this Bhagavad Gita classes in Balvi and all that, if you put in business, you can make lots of money. And my friends at Chinmay Mission said Rajan, as much time youre putting in your architectural practice if you put as much time in this. When I left Houston and I was completely immersed into this Vedanta, I had just come to United States, It has come to United States.
And I got inspired and started going to Gaurang Bais classes. So when I got a job and I said Gaurang bhai, I need to go to Dallas. So he said Rajan, then what will happen to all this? I said Gaurang bhai, I have only one desire to design high rise building.
And thats why I came to United States once I get this chance. Because I was working for a company which does nothing but high rise building. Or at least I got a job.
He said, once I fulfill my desire, Im going to focus on this. Its never going to happen. And its true, Im continue to practice architecture.
So should I really now consider that Im going to be lost from both sides?

Krishnas response in verse 40 is profoundly reassuring: Partha naiveha namutra vinashas tasya vidyate - My dear child, there is no destruction for this person, either in this world or the next. Na hi kalyana-krit kashchid durgatim tata gacchati - one who does good never comes to grief. This is a universal guarantee: sincere spiritual effort is never wasted. Even if you do not reach the goal in this lifetime, the progress you make is preserved and continued.
The mechanism is explained in verses 41-42: the yoga-bhrashta (one fallen from yoga) either takes birth in a pure and prosperous family where conditions support continued practice, or - even more rarely - in a family of wise yogis where spiritual progress can resume immediately. The second birth is described as durlabhataram - more difficult to obtain. This reveals the value of being born into a spiritually oriented family; such a birth is the result of significant previous effort.
The concept of spiritual bank balance is illuminating. If you retire and move to another country, your wealth comes with you. Similarly, the development of your inner instrument - the purification of mind and intellect, the wisdom gained, the vasanas refined - transfers to your next life. This is why child prodigies exist: mathematical geniuses and musical virtuosos are not accidents but continuations of development from previous lives. Today, take comfort in this assurance. Every moment of sincere practice, every genuine attempt to control the mind, every act of selfless service is deposited in an account that can never be lost. What investment could be more secure?
